That exact tag literally contains the substring `https://`, so rule 2's required content directly violates rule 1's prohibition. The only ways I can see to make the two rules "pass" both involve gaming the letter of the check rather than actually meeting it, e.g.:

- Hiding the string in a comment or inert location just to satisfy a naive grep - same problem, it's deceptive compliance, not real compliance, and the kiosks reportedly have no network anyway, so the tag would just fail to load.

3. Something else, e.g. bundling `aw.js` locally so no external URL is needed at all (removes the contradiction only if the exact-tag requirement is also dropped/updated).
